title: Spatial Dashboard Builder: Maps That Summarise
description: View capped OSM node counts and optional elevation for a chosen circular area.
summary_sentence: This fixed dashboard counts at most 3,000 returned OSM nodes; it is not an official statistics report.
quick_answer: Choose a centre and radius to display fixed counts for selected OSM node tags and an Open-Meteo centre elevation when available. Counts are capped and omit ways and relations; they are not official statistics.
steps_intro: A map alone is a picture; a dashboard is a picture with its evidence attached:

body.t: Facilities, coverage and counts by area in one shareable view — the format public meetings actually absorb. The underlying point patterns can be pre-mapped with the
Territories, depots and demand on one screen for the Monday meeting — a dashboard that updates its story when the data does.
The map-plus-numbers page is the modern data story. Panels force the author to state totals the map alone could insinuate.
Students who must summarise their own map stop trusting pretty choropleths blindly — building the dashboard is the lesson.

examples.label: Example · The panel disciplines the map

body.t: A heat blob looks alarming until its panel says '14 incidents, city of 900,000'. Dashboards that show counts beside colours are how spatial honesty is enforced in practice.
Counts per district versus rates per 10,000 residents tell different stories about the same points. A good dashboard states which it shows — and the population tools here supply the denominators.

popular_table.title: Dashboard anatomy
popular_table.intro: The parts and what each one owes the reader.
rows: Geography at a stated zoom and extent
Totals and breakdowns with their source named
Honest interactivity — what is excluded, stated
Dataset, provider and date — the dashboard's conscience
popular_table.note: This builder assembles views from open map data; it is a presentation layer, not a statistics authority. The base FAQ's 'official statistics?' question is answered by the source line you ship with it.
